United started brightly, pressing high and forcing early errors from a home defence that looked rattled by the intensity. The visitors carved out the game's first clear opening inside twelve minutes, when a driving run down the right released the overlapping full-back, whose low cross was turned narrowly wide at the near post.

The pressure told on **26 minutes**. A patient build-up through midfield ended with a slide-rule pass splitting the centre-backs, and United's forward finished coolly across the goalkeeper to open the scoring. It was no more than the visitors deserved.

The hosts responded with a spell of possession that yielded little, their build-up too ponderous against a compact defensive block. United nearly doubled the lead before the interval, striking the post from the edge of the area after a swift counter.

## The Equaliser and a Tactical Reshape

The complexion changed after the break. The home manager introduced a second holding midfielder for a struggling winger, tightening the centre and allowing his full-backs to push higher. The adjustment shifted momentum decisively.

The equaliser arrived on **63 minutes**. A whipped delivery from the left caught United's defence static, and an unmarked header from close range beat the goalkeeper. The home crowd, subdued for an hour, roared their side back into the tie.

United's manager reacted swiftly, withdrawing an attacking midfielder for a more disciplined ball-winner and instructing his side to slow the tempo. The change steadied the visitors, who reasserted a measure of control in the closing twenty minutes without seriously threatening a winner.

## Bookings and Flashpoints

Referee discipline was tested throughout a bad-tempered second half. Three yellow cards were shown to the home side—two for cynical fouls halting United counters, one for dissent—while United collected two cautions of their own, including one for their captain that rules him out of a portion of the return leg should he tread carelessly again. A late scramble in the box drew furious penalty appeals from the visitors, waved away by the referee.

## Chances Tally

- **United:** two clear-cut chances (one goal, one off the post), plus several half-openings from wide areas.
- **Hosts:** one clear-cut chance converted, with limited threat otherwise.

The expected-goals reading would favour the visitors, underlining a sense of opportunity missed.

## Implications for Old Trafford

United go home level, holding a valuable away goal and the comfort of a raucous home crowd for the decisive leg. A score draw or any victory sees them through; a goalless stalemate would force extra time.

The concern for United's manager will be the ease with which the equaliser was conceded and the caution to a key player. For the hosts, the second-half revival offers genuine belief—but they must find the attacking spark that eluded them for long periods here.

**The tie remains delicately poised. Old Trafford will decide it.**
